title: Choose the visual world for Illini Fantasy Hoops
question: The roll assigned The Rafters: the league hung like the program's banners at State Farm Center. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Rafters
options.lineage: Big Ten title and retired-jersey banners hung in the State Farm Center rafters
options.thesis: Every fantasy team is a banner, and the league is the row of banners overhead.
options.viewport: Top nav, then a rafter strip of all teams' banners ordered by standings with drop length = points for; below it this week's matchups, yours lifted, the rest dimmed a step.
options.risk: Banners are a signature for the league view; on dense tables the world must recede to type and palette or it turns into costume.

raised.raise: Rank by weight and case, not a ladder of sizes: one reading size for every table.
The open matchup lifts; every other banner and card dims a step behind it.
A banner's drop is an exact quantity (points for), never a decorative length.
State by form as well as hue: actual points solid-stitched, projections dashed, a final double-stitched.
The season reads as one line of weeks: past filled, this week lit, the rest outlined.

options.label: Block I
options.thesis: The league dressed exactly as the program dresses itself: Block I, Illini Blue, Illinois Orange.
options.viewport: Illini Blue header with the Block I, a white working ground, orange as the committed color for scores and your team.
options.risk: The most familiar option: it will read like the official athletics site, polished but expected.

options.label: Departure Board
options.lineage: airport boarding pass and live gate board
options.thesis: The week as a live board: players rerank in place as they score, and a change stays lit until you've seen it.
options.viewport: A ranked board of every player in your matchup, reordering live by points; your team as a segmented pass beside it.
options.case: Wins on clarity for live game nights; loses on identification: nothing in it is Illinois.
options.risk: Strongest during games, thin on the quiet days and before the season.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.thesis: Sections as colored tab boards with acetate leaves.
options.viewport: Tab rail down the edge, one section per tab.
options.case: Staff don't recognise themselves in a manual; tabs fight standard navigation.
options.kept: One reading size does the work.

options.label: Title Wall
options.thesis: Players as poster tiles that expand on focus.
options.viewport: Rows of headshot tiles by position.
options.case: Hides the numbers staff want until you focus a tile.
options.risk: Reads as entertainment, not a league.
options.kept: The focused item lifts; the rest dim.

options.label: Transit Diagram
options.thesis: The season drawn as rail lines and interchanges.
options.viewport: Teams as lines crossing at matchups.
options.case: A clever map of something nobody needs to navigate.
options.kept: The season as one line of stations.

options.label: Dance Score
options.thesis: Time runs upward; length is exact duration.
options.case: Foreign notation for a basketball staff.

options.label: Emission Rail
options.thesis: Everything hangs off one calibrated rail; state is line form.
options.case: Too abstract for a league; no Illinois in it.
options.risk: Austere to the point of opaque.
options.kept: State by form, not only hue.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark fantasy dashboard like Sleeper or ESPN Fantasy, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Matchup scoreboard first, standings and news beside it.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the apps everyone already has; close to what the site is today.
